```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(gridExtra)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

### Loading the dataset

```{r}
df = read.delim("housing-prices-ge19.txt")
```

### Looking at the pattern of missing data

```{r}
visdat::vis_miss(df) + coord_flip() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

=\> No data is missing

### Data dictionary

I am using the data dictionary of the [SaratogaHouses: Houses in Saratoga County (2006) dataset](https://rdrr.io/cran/mosaicData/man/SaratogaHouses.html) (Pruim et al., 2023) to interpret the meanings and units of variables in this dataset, following the instruction from [this comment](https://edstem.org/au/courses/25836/discussion/2948658?answer=6509453) on Ed Discussion (Lauer, 2025).

### Distribution of dependent variable (house price)

```{r, message=FALSE}
Q1_Price <- quantile(df$Price, 0.25)
Q3_Price <- quantile(df$Price, 0.75)
IQR_Price <- Q3_Price - Q1_Price
lower_bound_Price <- Q1_Price - 1.5 * IQR_Price
upper_bound_Price <- Q3_Price + 1.5 * IQR_Price

ggplot(df, aes(x=Price)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "House Price (USD)") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))

ggplot(df, aes(x=Price)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(x = "House Price (USD)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))  +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lower_bound_Price, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = lower_bound_Price + 75000, y = 250, label = paste0("Lower bound"))  +
  geom_vline(xintercept = upper_bound_Price, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = upper_bound_Price + 75000, y = 250, label = paste0("Upper bound")) 
# ggplot(df, aes(x=Price,
#           y = after_stat(density))) + 
#       geom_histogram() + 
#       labs(x = "House Price", 
#            y = "Probability") +
#   scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +
#   scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))  +
#   geom_vline(xintercept = lower_bound_Price, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1)  +

      # theme(axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14,

      #       axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14,
      #                                   margin = margin(r = 15)),
      #       axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)))
```

=\> Right-skewed distribution

### Reclassification to factor variables

```{r}
categorical_vars = c("Fuel.Type", "Heat.Type", "Sewer.Type")
df <- df %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(unname(categorical_vars)), as.factor))

# Boolean variables
boolean_vars = c("Waterfront", "New.Construct", "Central.Air")
df <- df %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(unname(boolean_vars)), as.factor))
```

### Dependent variable against potential predictors

Included in EDA submission

#### [Price vs Living Area/ Bedroom]{.underline}

```{r} p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x=Living.Area, y = Price)) +        geom_point() +        labs(x = "Living.Area (square feet)",             y = "Price (USD)") +   scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))  df$Bedroom.Living.Area = df$Living.Area / df$Bedrooms p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Bedroom.Living.Area, y = Price)) +   geom_point() +   labs(x = "Living.Area.Per.Bedroom (square feet)",             y = "Price (USD)") +   scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))  grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol=2)}
```

The lot size seems to be pretty left-skewed?

#### [Price vs Central.Air (Faceted by Waterfront)]{.underline}

```{r}
ggplot(df) + aes(y = New.Construct, x = Price) + 
  geom_boxplot() +   
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) + 
  facet_grid( Waterfront ~ .)
```

### Dependent variable against other independent variables

```

=\> Not normal or linear =\> Might need to put into graph/table with another categorical factor to see what happens

#### [Price vs Lot.Size]{.underline}

Remove outliers from Lot.Size

```{r}
ggplotly(ggplot(df, aes(y=Lot.Size)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)))

Q1_LotSize <- quantile(df$Lot.Size, 0.25)
Q3_LotSize <- quantile(df$Lot.Size, 0.75)
IQR_LotSize <- Q3_LotSize - Q1_LotSize
lower_bound_LotSize <- Q1_LotSize - 1.5 * IQR_LotSize
upper_bound_LotSize <- Q3_LotSize + 1.5 * IQR_LotSize

cleaned_df_LotSize <- df %>%
  filter(Lot.Size >= lower_bound_LotSize & Lot.Size <= upper_bound_LotSize)

ggplot(cleaned_df_LotSize, aes(y=Lot.Size)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))
```

Visualise Price vs Lot.Size

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x=Lot.Size, y = Price)) + 
      geom_point() + 
      labs(x = "Size of lot (acres)", 
           y = "Price") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))  +
  geom_vline(xintercept = upper_bound_LotSize, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1)

ggplot(cleaned_df_LotSize, aes(x=Lot.Size, y = Price)) + 
      geom_point() + 
      labs(title = "Scatterplot without outliers",
           x = "Size of lot (acres)", 
           y = "Price") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))
```

With outlier: pretty hard to see any pattern. Without outlier: looks pretty random.

#### [Price vs Land.Value]{.underline}

Distribution of Land.Value

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Land.Value)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))

Q1_LandVal <- quantile(df$Land.Value, 0.25)
Q3_LandVal <- quantile(df$Land.Value, 0.75)
IQR_LandVal <- Q3_LandVal - Q1_LandVal
lower_bound_LandVal <- Q1_LandVal - 1.5 * IQR_LandVal
upper_bound_LandVal <- Q3_LandVal + 1.5 * IQR_LandVal
```

Scatterplot of Price against Land.Value

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x=Land.Value, y = Price)) + 
      geom_point() + 
      labs(x = "Value of land (USD)", 
           y = "Price") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = upper_bound_LandVal, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))

df %>%
  filter(Land.Value >= lower_bound_LandVal & Land.Value <= upper_bound_LandVal) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Land.Value, y = Price)) + 
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Scatterplot without outliers",
       x = "Value of land (USD)",
       y = "Price") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))
```

May fit linear model

#### [Price vs Bedrooms]{.underline}

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Price, y = Bedrooms, group=Bedrooms)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE))
```

Does impact/ Does have a relation =\> Needs testing/ investigation

Mean of house price of house with:

-   1 bedroom: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 1])`

-   2 bedrooms: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 2])` -\> Decrease

-   3 bedrooms: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 3])` -\> Increase, close to that of 1 bedroom

Quite similar:

-   4 bedrooms: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 4])`

-   5 bedrooms: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 5])`

-   6 bedrooms: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 6])`

Decrease:

-   7 bedrooms: `r mean(df$Price[df$Bedrooms == 7])`
